source_caption:
Sully (2016) is a compelling biographical drama directed by Clint Eastwood. The story follows veteran commercial pilot Chesley "Sully" Sullenberger, who becomes an instant public hero after successfully executing an emergency landing of US Airways Flight 1549 on the freezing Hudson River, miraculously saving all 155 passengers and crew on board.

The plot unfolds in the immediate aftermath of the harrowing "Miracle on the Hudson". While the public and media shower Sully with praise, a rigorous National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) investigation threatens to destroy his reputation and career. Computer simulations suggest he could have safely returned to an airport rather than risking a water landing. Sully must defend his split-second decision-making while grappling with post-traumatic stress, intrusive media scrutiny, and deep self-doubt.

Beyond the mechanical recount of an aviation crisis, the film explores profound themes of accountability, leadership under pressure, human instinct versus institutional algorithms, and personal integrity. It contrasts rigid, cold data analysis against the priceless value of human experience and judgment during moments of extreme chaos.

Through a grounded narrative analysis, the movie presents a powerful examination of quiet heroics and professional dedication. It demonstrates that true leadership lies not in seeking glory, but in remaining calm, relying on decades of preparation, and taking total responsibility for the lives entrusted to your care.

What makes Sully more than just a typical disaster reconstruction is its intimate focus on psychological resilience and collective humanity. It elevates a world-famous news story into a moving meditation on duty, humility, and the extraordinary power of everyday people coming together in a crisis.

When crisis strikes, can computer algorithms ever replace the human instinct and experience required to make life-or-death choices?

source_details.synopsis: Sully (also known as Sully: Miracle on the Hudson) is a 2016 American biographical drama film directed by Clint Eastwood and written by Todd Komarnicki, based on the 2009 autobiography Highest Duty by Chesley "Sully" Sullenberger and Jeffrey Skiles. Tom Hanks stars as Sullenberger, with Aaron Eckhart as Jeffrey Skiles, and co-stars Laura Linney, Anna Gunn, Autumn Reeser, Holt McCallany, and Jamey Sheridan. The film follows "Sully" Sullenberger's 2009 emergency landing of US Airways Flight 1549 on the Hudson River, in which all 155 passengers and crew survived, and the subsequent publicity and investigation.
